text: Rule 1. Every proposal must be preceded by a critical capability assessment, if both that proposal is classified as "first_deployment" and that proposal is frontier.

Rule 1. Every proposal need not be preceded by a critical capability assessment, if both that proposal is classified as "low_risk" and that proposal is classified as "governance_found_acceptable_with_safety_case_where_ccl_reached".

Rule 1. Every proposal must be preceded by a determination of any substantial modification, if all of the following hold: (a) that proposal is subsequent; (b) both that proposal is classified as "new_capabilities" and that proposal is classified as "could_undermine_justification".

Rule 1. Every proposal must be preceded by a determination of any further capability assessment needed, if all of the following hold: (a) that proposal is subsequent; (b) both that proposal is classified as "new_capabilities" and that proposal is classified as "could_undermine_justification".
Rule 1. Every proposal must be preceded by a determination of any substantial modification, if that proposal is subsequent.
Rule 1. Every proposal must be preceded by a determination of any further capability assessment needed, if that proposal is subsequent.

Rule 1. Every proposal must be preceded by a further critical capability assessment, if all of the following hold: (a) that proposal is subsequent; (b) both that proposal is classified as "new_capabilities" and that proposal is classified as "could_undermine_justification".
Rule 1. Every proposal must be followed by material capability change assessments on various checkpoints, if that proposal is classified as "post_training_run_completed".
Rule 1. Every proposal must be followed by an assessment of proximity to each level with a risk analysis, if both that proposal approaches that level and that level is critical.

Rule 1. Every proposal must be subject to residual risk assessments in evaluating deployment mitigations, if there is a level such that all of the following hold: (a) that proposal has reached that level; (b) either that level is tracked or that level is critical, or both.
Rule 1. Every proposal must have its residual risk assessment informed by a safety case, if there is a level such that both that proposal has reached that level and that level is critical.
Rule 1. Every proposal is acceptable, if it is not the case that there is a level such that that proposal has reached that level.

Rule 1. Every proposal is acceptable, if all of the following hold: (a) there is a level such that both that proposal has reached that level and that level is misuse; (b) for every level that is misuse and that that proposal has reached, all of the following hold: (i) if that proposal is external, then that proposal mitigates that level; (ii) at least one of the following holds: (a) there is a measure such that both that level recommends that measure and that proposal applies that measure; (b) either that proposal is classified as "security_assessed_adequate" or that proposal is classified as "open_release_benefits_outweigh_risks", or both.

Rule 1. Every proposal must have mitigations make the residual risk of harm acceptable, if all of the following hold: (a) that proposal is external; (b) there is a level such that both that proposal has reached that level and that level is misuse.

Rule 1. Every proposal must have security mitigations that reach the recommended security level, if there is a level such that both that proposal has reached that level and that level is misuse, unless either that proposal is classified as "security_assessed_adequate" or that proposal is classified as "open_release_benefits_outweigh_risks", or both.

Rule 1. Every proposal need not have mitigations make the residual risk of harm acceptable, if all of the following hold: (a) either that proposal is internal or that proposal is classified as "further_development", or both; (b) there is a level such that both that proposal has reached that level and that level is misuse.

Rule 1. Every proposal is acceptable, if all of the following hold: (a) there is a level such that all of the following hold: (i) that proposal has reached that level; (ii) both that level is critical and that level is classified as "ml_rd_and_misalignment"; (b) for every level that is critical and that that proposal has reached, if that level is classified as "ml_rd_and_misalignment", then all of the following hold: (i) if either that proposal is external or that proposal is classified as "high_risk", or both, then that proposal mitigates that level; (ii) at least one of the following holds: (a) there is a measure such that both that level recommends that measure and that proposal applies that measure; (b) either that proposal is classified as "security_assessed_adequate" or that proposal is classified as "open_release_benefits_outweigh_risks", or both.

Rule 1. Every proposal must have mitigations make the residual risk of severe harm acceptable, if all of the following hold: (a) either that proposal is external or that proposal is classified as "high_risk", or both; (b) there is a level such that all of the following hold: (i) that proposal has reached that level; (ii) both that level is critical and that level is classified as "ml_rd_and_misalignment".

Rule 1. Every proposal must have security mitigations that reach the recommended security level, if there is a level such that all of the following hold: (a) that proposal has reached that level; (b) both that level is critical and that level is classified as "ml_rd_and_misalignment", unless either that proposal is classified as "security_assessed_adequate" or that proposal is classified as "open_release_benefits_outweigh_risks", or both.

Rule 1. Every proposal need not have mitigations make the residual risk of severe harm acceptable, if all of the following hold: (a) at least one of the following holds: (i) that proposal is classified as "further_development"; (ii) all of the following hold: (a) that proposal is internal; (b) it is not the case that that proposal is classified as "high_risk"; (b) there is a level such that all of the following hold: (i) that proposal has reached that level; (ii) both that level is critical and that level is classified as "ml_rd_and_misalignment".

Rule 1. Every proposal is acceptable, if there is a level such that all of the following hold: (a) all of the following hold: (i) that proposal has reached that level; (ii) both that level is tracked and that level is classified as "ml_rd_and_misalignment"; (b) all of the following hold: (i) if either that proposal is external or that proposal is classified as "high_risk", or both, then either that proposal mitigates that level or that proposal is classified as "unlikely_misalignment_propensities", or both; (ii) either that proposal is classified as "security_assessed_adequate" or that proposal is classified as "open_release_benefits_outweigh_risks", or both.

Rule 1. Every proposal must have mitigations make the residual risk of significant harm acceptable, if all of the following hold: (a) either that proposal is external or that proposal is classified as "high_risk", or both; (b) there is a level such that all of the following hold: (i) that proposal has reached that level; (ii) both that level is tracked and that level is classified as "ml_rd_and_misalignment", unless that proposal is classified as "unlikely_misalignment_propensities".

Rule 1. Every proposal must have a level of security assessed as adequate, if there is a level such that all of the following hold: (a) that proposal has reached that level; (b) both that level is tracked and that level is classified as "ml_rd_and_misalignment", unless that proposal is classified as "open_release_benefits_outweigh_risks".

Rule 1. Every proposal need not have mitigations make the residual risk of significant harm acceptable, if all of the following hold: (a) at least one of the following holds: (i) that proposal is classified as "further_development"; (ii) all of the following hold: (a) that proposal is internal; (b) it is not the case that that proposal is classified as "high_risk"; (b) there is a level such that all of the following hold: (i) that proposal has reached that level; (ii) both that level is tracked and that level is classified as "ml_rd_and_misalignment".

Rule 1. Every proposal must not proceed, if all of the following hold: (a) that proposal is external; (b) there is a level such that both that proposal has reached that level and that level is misuse, unless that proposal is classified as "governance_found_acceptable_with_safety_case_where_ccl_reached".
Rule 1. Every proposal must not proceed, if that proposal is external, unless that proposal is classified as "governance_found_acceptable_with_safety_case_where_ccl_reached".

Rule 1. Every proposal must not proceed, if all of the following hold: (a) either that proposal is external or that proposal is classified as "high_risk", or both; (b) there is a level such that both that proposal has reached that level and that level is classified as "ml_rd_and_misalignment", unless that proposal is classified as "governance_found_acceptable_with_safety_case_where_ccl_reached".

Rule 1. Every proposal must not proceed, if either that proposal is external or that proposal is classified as "high_risk", or both, unless that proposal is classified as "governance_found_acceptable_with_safety_case_where_ccl_reached".
Rule 1. Every proposal must be submitted to review by the appropriate governance function, if that proposal is classified as "material_safety_case_update".
Rule 1. Every proposal need not add mitigations against insider misuse beyond the baseline controls, if there is a level such that both that proposal has reached that level and that level is misuse.

Rule 1. Every proposal should apply each measure to the model weights, if there is a level such that all of the following hold: (a) that proposal has reached that level; (b) at least one of the following holds: (i) that level recommends that measure; (ii) there is a second measure such that both that level recommends the second measure and the second measure includes that measure.

Rule 1. Every proposal must apply each measure to the model weights, if there is a level such that all of the following hold: (a) that proposal has reached that level; (b) at least one of the following holds: (i) that level recommends that measure; (ii) there is a second measure such that both that level recommends the second measure and the second measure includes that measure.

Rule 1. Every proposal must be subject to periodic residual risk assessments of misalignment risk, if there is a level such that all of the following hold: (a) that proposal has reached that level; (b) both that level is tracked and that level is classified as "ml_rd_and_misalignment".

Rule 1. Every proposal must have its periodic assessments cover high-risk internal deployments, if there is a level such that all of the following hold: (a) that proposal has reached that level; (b) both that level is tracked and that level is classified as "ml_rd_and_misalignment".

Rule 1. Every proposal must have the additional safeguards applied, if all of the following hold: (a) both that proposal is internal and that proposal is classified as "internal_risk_unacceptable_without_safeguards"; (b) there is a level such that all of the following hold: (i) that proposal has reached that level; (ii) both that level is tracked and that level is classified as "ml_rd_and_misalignment".
Rule 1. Every proposal must be covered by a review of the framework at least once a year.
Rule 1. Every proposal must be covered by a more frequent review of the framework, if that proposal is classified as "adherence_undermined".

Rule 1. Every proposal should share relevant information with appropriate government authorities, if all of the following hold: (a) there is a level such that both that proposal has reached that level and that level is critical; (b) both that proposal is classified as "unmitigated_public_safety_risk" and that proposal is classified as "sharing_facilitates_safety".
Rule 1. Every proposal must have holistically assessed mitigations proportionate with expected impact.
Rule 1. Every proposal should have holistically assessed mitigations proportionate with expected impact.
Rule 1. Every proposal must have its residual risk brought within the acceptable levels.
Rule 1. Every proposal should have its residual risk brought within the acceptable levels.
Rule 1. Every proposal must have its risk assessment conservatively weigh greater elicitation by others.
Rule 1. Every proposal should have its risk assessment conservatively weigh greater elicitation by others.
